about: Authored query pairs for tools/sample_db_bench.py. Labels are under the declared Employees primary and foreign keys; each different pair has a legal separating database.

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: employees.emp_no is the declared primary key

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the primary key two employees may share an employee number

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: dept_emp.emp_no is a non-null foreign key to the employee primary key, so each row matches exactly one employee
pairs.left: SELECT de.emp_no, de.dept_no FROM dept_emp AS de JOIN employees AS e ON e.emp_no = de.emp_no

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the foreign key a department assignment can name a missing employee
pairs.left: SELECT de.emp_no, de.dept_no FROM dept_emp AS de JOIN employees AS e ON e.emp_no = de.emp_no

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: salaries.emp_no is a non-null foreign key to the employee primary key and no employee column is read
pairs.left: SELECT s.emp_no, s.from_date FROM salaries AS s LEFT JOIN employees AS e ON e.emp_no = s.emp_no

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: employees.emp_no is non-null by its primary key

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: titles.to_date is nullable, so COUNT(to_date) can skip a row

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: one legal male row appears only in the first query
pairs.left: SELECT emp_no FROM employees WHERE gender = 'M'
pairs.right: SELECT emp_no FROM employees WHERE gender = 'F'
